title: Structured decision chronicle to improve routing debuggability and replayability
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a compact, human-readable 'decision chronicle' artifact emitted per request that records the sequence of routing decisions (region selection, tier routing, fallback model variant) across hops. The chronicle should be optimized for storage and query, include a natural-language rationale summary, diffs of context/constraints per hop, and replay hooks to reconstruct the exact inputs for downstream RCA and regression testing.
acceptance_criteria: Agent can query a chronicle by request_id and see chronological hop entries with timestamp, selected node/region/tier, chosen model variant, and a short automated rationale (<=280 chars)
Chronicle size budget: 95th percentile < 3KB per sampled request and worst-case < 32KB when full artifacts are attached
Reconstruction API: an internal /replay endpoint accepts chronicle_id and returns the sanitized replay bundle (model tags, pinned version, routing policy snapshot) for deterministic replay in staging
Sampling controls: admins can set global sampling rate, per-customer sampling, and cost-aware downsampling for high-throughput customers

Retention & query: chronicle entries are ingested into trace-store with 30d full retention and 6mo compact index; queries by request_id, route_policy_id, region, and model_variant succeed under 500ms for 95% of requests
Privacy: chronicle attachments are redacted automatically using PII filters and honor KMS-encrypted storage for private deployments
implementation_notes: Emit a compact protobuf record per routing hop including fields: hop_index, ts_iso, chosen_region, chosen_tier, model_variant, latency_ms, policy_id, rationale_tokens (short summary), context_diff_hash, attach_artifact_url(optional)
Store full artifacts (prefix snapshots, policy JSON) in encrypted object storage and reference via signed short-lived URLs in chronicle when sampled for full capture
Integrate with existing trace pipeline (Zipkin/OTLP) but write chronicles to a dedicated index in OLAP store (e.g., ClickHouse) with materialized views for frequent queries
Add ReplayService API that accepts chronicle_id and returns sanitized deterministic bundle; support mode=staging (safe) and mode=diagnostic (full with auth)
Add Kafka topic 'routing-chronicles' with partitioning by customer_id to allow downstream join with metrics and cost-accounting sinks
Provide enrichment hooks: cost_estimate_per_hop, queued_tokens, and fallback_reason_code to assist alerting and SLO analysis
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): emit chronicle summaries (no attachments) at 0.1% global sampling in us-east-1 for 2 weeks; validate size and indexing
Phase 2 (controlled): enable per-customer 1% sampling and attach full artifacts for flagged customers (security-approved) in non-prod regions
Phase 3 (ramp): increase to 5% global sampling and enable cost-aware downsampling for top-10 tenants; enable replay endpoint in staging environments
Phase 4 (GA): default 0.5% sampling global, 30d full retention; expose query widgets in Console under 'Routing -> Chronicles' and link to request timelines
testing_plan: Unit tests: serialization/deserialization of chronicle proto, redaction pipeline tests
Load tests: validate 100K chronicle events/s write to Kafka and 20K inserts/s into ClickHouse with retention TTL enforcement
E2E tests: create synthetic multi-hop routing scenarios including region failover and verify replay returns identical routing decisions when run in deterministic mode
Security tests: KMS encryption/decryption round-trip for attachments; PII redaction fuzzing against sample corpus
Monitoring: create dashboards for chronicle emission rate, average chronicle size, storage cost per day, and replay latency
risks: Storage cost growth if sampling controls or redaction fail; mitigate with hard caps and adaptive downsampling
Sensitive data leakage if attachments are not redacted; require KMS + mandatory redaction rules before storage
Replay nondeterminism if dependent model artifacts change; mitigate by recording model_version and snapshotting minimal inputs
Query performance regressions as chronicle volume grows; use partitioned tables and TTL compaction to maintain QPS targets
